title: Turns out the real Qwen benchmark is whether it can pay for its own GPU. Running my Qwen 3.8 27B trading agent live 24/7.
author: artguerilla

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
the part that would worry me is not the trading, it's "keeps adjusting the strategy based on what actually happened". that is refitting to the last few days of noise, live, with positions open.

what bit us running a fleet round the clock was never a bad entry. it was the position that quietly never closed and sat there for a week while everything else looked fine.

replies.author: artguerilla
replies.body: well i try to use common sense and give it some boundries like right now its working on a 30 min span for trades, based on the Trends from m1 to m15. Right now im setting up a bit broader window aiming for up to 2hrs. So there's little to no chance it can forget about a position.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the short window helps inside a run. the one that got us was between runs: process restarts, fresh context, and the position from the previous window is not in it anywhere. worth having something outside the model that reconciles open positions against what it thinks it holds.

replies.author: artguerilla
replies.body: Yeah that's not fast enought. I have my agent running a python bot enforcing rules ans strats. Behind that runs a Hindsight memory and a obsidian second brain.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the bounded window is the right call. what bites later is the handoff, when a position opens inside one window and has to be understood by a run that never saw it open.

replies.author: artguerilla
replies.body: that should be easy to be adressed with a sqlite ledger that get injected before every order. run this deterministic within ms.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: A ledger fixes the model forgetting, sure. The one that got me was the row being read wrong on the way in: our spread symbols pack two expiry dates and a first-match regex grabbed the short leg, so a live diagonal got filed as expired. Deterministic, ran in milliseconds, still wrong.
